body.estimand_functional: \(I_n^{\mathrm{prof}}=\operatorname{hull}\{\vartheta\in\Theta:\inf_{c\in\mathcal G_c}\Delta_n(c,\vartheta)\le\Gamma_n(\delta_n)\}\). The proved minimax converse satisfies \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\ge F_{\alpha,s,M}(T_n)\) throughout \(0<\kappa_n\le1/8\), and \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\ge\max\{G_\alpha(\tau_n),F_{\alpha,s,M}(T_n)\}\) when \(\kappa_n\le1/16\); in particular, \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\gtrsim r_n\) over the full declared strength shell. The matching profile upper comparison \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\asymp r_n\) remains proposed only on \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{cert}}\).

sampling_model.design: Independent random design with \(X_i\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\) and an unknown law-specific cutoff \(c_P\in[1/4,3/4]\).
sampling_model.units: The observations are \(O_i=(X_i,D_i,Y_i)\), for \(i=1,\ldots,n\), with binary treatment and outcome.
sampling_model.treatment: The instrument is \(Z_i=\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge c_P\}\), and monotone response types imply \(D_i=D_i(Z_i)\).
sampling_model.overlap: The compliance jump lies in \([\kappa_n,2\kappa_n]\). The main class imposes no outcome-variance, residual-variance, covariance-eigenvalue, or joint-cell positivity floor; every binary treatment--outcome association compatible with the observable margins and causal model is allowed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Separate one-sided radius-\(M\), order-\(s\) H\"older extensions are imposed only on the observable treatment and outcome margins. Association is a free binwise Fr\'echet coordinate. A four-cell method-of-types threshold gives finite-sample calibration on certified grids, and the rule returns the full parameter space on each enumerated fallback branch.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their unknown-threshold result transfers the minimax rate for estimating a sharp-RD discontinuity location from a convolution white-noise model.
Their moderate-break analysis derives a Gaussian-process limit experiment and a nearly weighted-average-power maximizing test.
Their Theorem 1 gives uniformly asymptotically valid conditional tests with a functional nuisance parameter.
Their Theorem 1 shows that risk functions attainable in the weak-GMM Gaussian-process experiment bound finite-sample asymptotic risk.
Their Theorem 3.1 characterizes optimal one-sided confidence intervals through an ordered modulus over convex fixed-index regression classes.
Their sharp testable implications for fuzzy-RD validity are inequalities in the joint outcome--treatment distribution at the cutoff.
Their LoTTA model propagates posterior uncertainty about an unknown cutoff into fuzzy-RD effect estimation.
Their main unknown-discontinuity theory treats testing and estimation in sharp RD, with fuzzy RD discussed separately.

body.tldr: For fuzzy regression discontinuity with a weak compliance jump and unknown cutoff, cutoff recovery and causal-effect informativeness are distinct. Integrating the moving-cutoff continuum gives the explicit lower value \(G_\alpha(\tau_n)\), while integrating the causal-valid fixed-cutoff bump continuum gives the new exact envelope \(F_{\alpha,s,M}(T_n)\). Thus \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\ge F_{\alpha,s,M}(T_n)\) at every declared strength, \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\ge\max\{G_\alpha(\tau_n),F_{\alpha,s,M}(T_n)\}\) when \(\kappa_n\le1/16\), and \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\gtrsim r_n\) globally under the unchanged binary H{\"o}lder-margin class. Finite-grid four-cell calibration remains valid for every compatible treatment--outcome association, including singular cells. The support-wide profile upper bound, attainment, the \(s=1\) finite-positive critical decision value, and full-model least favorability remain open.

project_justification.gap: Known-cutoff weak-fuzzy inference, sharp-RD unknown-cutoff rates, generic weak-identification decision theory, and Bayesian propagation of cutoff uncertainty have been developed separately. None supplies the two integrated label-wise lower envelopes, an all-strength minimax converse, and an attaining honest connected interval when the cutoff and fuzzy denominator weaken jointly; the lower side is proved here, whereas attainment remains open.
project_justification.niche: The preserved binary uniform-design class makes two complementary causal lifts explicit while leaving the observable treatment--outcome association unrestricted. The moving-cutoff continuum measures slope-location ambiguity through \(G_\alpha(\tau_n)\), and the fixed-cutoff compact-bump continuum measures ordinary nonparametric jump difficulty through \(F_{\alpha,s,M}(T_n)\).
project_justification.fill: The project integrates both legal continua to prove \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\ge F_{\alpha,s,M}(T_n)\) throughout the strength shell, the maximum of \(F_{\alpha,s,M}\) and \(G_\alpha\) on the moving-family range, and the coarse all-strength converse \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\gtrsim r_n\). It also defines a support-wide four-cell profile and proves exact finite-grid calibration while leaving association free. The matching upper frontier, complete critical experiment, exact finite-positive decision values, and a total attaining interval remain unresolved.

body.related_work: Hahn, Todd, and van der Klaauw (2001) supply the local Wald identification argument. Feir, Lemieux, and Marmer (2016) and Noack and Rothe (2024, Theorem 1) give weak-identification-robust inference at a fixed known cutoff; they inform the exact singleton-cutoff finite-grid calibration and reduction proved here, but no first-order residual-jump equivalence is claimed. The integrated fixed-cutoff bump continuum sharpens the lower analysis to the explicit value function \(F_{\alpha,s,M}(T_n)\), while the moving-cutoff continuum supplies the distinct \(1/(n\kappa_n^3)\) difficulty and explicit value \(G_\alpha(\tau_n)\). Porter and Yu (2015, Sections 3--5) and Tuvaandorj (2020, Sections 3--4) study unknown-location behavior predominantly in sharp designs, without this weak causal ratio or connected honest-length criterion. Elliott and M{\"u}ller (2014, Sections 2.1--2.3) motivate process experiments for moderate unknown breaks, but do not solve the present H{\"o}lder-margin decision problem. Andrews and Mikusheva (2016, Theorem 1) and Andrews and Mikusheva (2022, Theorem 1 and Section 4) inform nuisance calibration and weak-decision analysis; Armstrong and Koles{\'a}r (2018, Theorem 3.1 and Appendix A.4) connect testing power to expected length over convex fixed-index classes. None proves the still-open support-wide profile upper bound over the translated nonconvex union. Arai, Hsu, Kitagawa, Mourifi{\'e}, and Wan (2022, Section 2) motivate retaining the full joint outcome--treatment law. Kowalska, van de Wiel, and van der Pas (2025 version, Sections 3 and 6) propagate unknown-cutoff uncertainty in a Bayesian model without uniform frequentist honesty or minimax length.
body.technical_internal_limitation: A product of the two marginal Bernoulli likelihoods is not the likelihood of the observed pair when association is unrestricted. The finite-grid calibration therefore uses the complete binned four-cell vector and a method-of-types threshold that remains valid on singular cell faces. Its dimension cost \(\zeta_n\) need not be negligible on every sequence satisfying cutoff recovery; \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{cert}}\) is only the proposed domain for a conservative finite-grid upper-rate comparison, and no profile upper rate has yet been proved there. Separately, an untruncated second moment of a translated-cutoff mixture does not determine a critical constant; boundary truncation, mixture renormalization, the signed effect label, and second-order centering must remain in the experiment.
body.honest_scope: The model has no outcome-variance, null-residual-variance, covariance-eigenvalue, or joint-cell positivity floor, and the strengthened lower bound adds none. The proved lower results include the moving-cutoff causal lift and its Kullback--Leibler bound, the explicit integrated value \(G_\alpha(\tau_n)\), the fixed-cutoff compact-bump causal lift and its \(n(\kappa_n|u|)^{2+1/s}\) divergence bound, the exact integrated fixed-cutoff envelope \(F_{\alpha,s,M}(T_n)\), and the all-strength converse \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\gtrsim r_n\). Exact singleton-cutoff finite-grid four-cell calibration and population false-split separation are also proved uniformly over permitted binary treatment--outcome associations. These facts do not establish continuum honesty, an upper expected-length rate, or attainment by \(I_n^{\mathrm{prof}}\). The finite-positive decision values, full-model least favorability, continuum discretization, localized stochastic profile bound, and negligible fallback risk remain open. A matching upper comparison is only a proposed goal on \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{cert}}\). No smoothness of joint cells, conditional independence for the full class, association separation, cross-side derivative matching, oracle cutoff, or known association nuisance is imposed.
